Subject: MPO - private offer term options & buyer approval path for AcmeHealth

Hi Ben / Acme procurement,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really appreciated the time. Per our conversation I’m attaching a short private-offer sketch with three structured options (pilot -> 12mo delegated activation -> 36mo enterprise commit). The key questions we need to resolve to put a private offer into AWS Marketplace are:

- Term length the buyer is willing to sign for (12 / 24 / 36 months)
- Who in Acme can approve the purchase (procurement only / delegated BU approver / CFO/legal required)
- Whether you need invoice net-60 vs net-30 and any annual true-up language

Can you confirm who will be the decision owner for the final contract and the expected timeline to route the PO internally? If helpful I can propose two private-offer configurations that map to your approval lanes.

Attached: Redwood_Private_Offer_Options_20261002.pdf (summary of options + activation steps).

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm decision owner, 2) pick Option A/B/C below, 3) we draft the private offer and send PO instructions to procurement.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: MPO - private offer term options & buyer approval path for AcmeHealth

Jordan — thanks, doc received. A few clarifying items from procurement and our finance lead:

1) Split across BU: Acme has two business units that will consume this (CareOps + Analytics). Can the private offer be structured so each BU issues their own PO against the same private-offer id, or do we need a single consolidated PO?

2) Approval thresholds: Procurement can route up to $150k without CFO signature. Anything above that requires CFO sign-off (Sara Cho). If the committed value is >$150k we’ll need to involve legal and finance.

3) Pilot ask: Our product team would like an initial paid pilot (3 months) before committing to multi-year. Is that supported in the private offer flow? Ideally a 3-month paid pilot that rolls into a 36-month private offer upon acceptance.

4) Invoice terms: Finance prefers net-60 for pilots and mid-market pilots; later we can move to net-30 for enterprise commits. Is that feasible?

We’ve attached our internal PO template for reference (Acme_PO_Template.docx). I’m copying Sara so she’s aware — she’ll be the approver if the number crosses threshold. Timeline: procurement can review and route in ~5 business days once we have a concrete option.

–Ben
Ben Lowe
Sr. Manager, Procurement — AcmeHealth
ben@acmehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MPO - private offer term options & buyer approval path for AcmeHealth

Jordan / Marissa — quick runbook based on Ben’s notes. High level guidance for AWS MPO and buyer routing:

- Multi-PO against same MPO ID: Supported if each PO references the MPO offer id and the seller accepts multiple activations. We should explicitly call this out in the offer instructions so Procurement can create separate POs per BU. Advantage: keeps committed spend aligned to each BU and avoids CFO needing to sign each smaller PO if under threshold.

- Approval thresholds: If total expected ARR/commit could exceed $150k, plan for CFO/legal involvement. We can present two configurations:
  * Delegated activation (Option D): 12-month private offer, up to $150k per PO, procurement signs — no CFO required.
  * Enterprise commit (Option E): 36-month with consolidated commitment >$150k, requires CFO & legal, includes a 10% volume discount and SLA addendum.

- Pilot flow: Pilot -> convert to MPO. We can create a short (3mo) paid pilot using a limited-duration MPO or vendor invoice (credit) that converts into the long-term MPO. Operationally easiest: issue a PO for the pilot and include clear conversion instructions (PO reference + acceptance link). Note: AWS Marketplace requires the MPO seller to accept the offer; provide acceptance template and PO instructions.

- Invoice terms: Net-60 for pilot is fine; enterprise commitments default to net-30. We can include a one-time invoice-term exception in the private-offer notes (will need finance approval).

I’ll draft two concrete MPO payloads to mirror Option D & E and include explicit PO instructions and acceptance text. Jordan — can you confirm the estimated $ value so we can pick the right lane? Also add any notes about expected start date so we can set activation windows.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Marketplace & Partnerships — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Lowe <ben@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MPO - private offer term options & buyer approval path for AcmeHealth

Ben — thanks for the clarity; appreciate the PO template. Quick proposal to make routing straightforward (picking from Karthik’s guidance):

Option A — 12mo delegated activation (procurement approval only)
- Each BU issues own PO referencing MPO id
- Per-PO cap: $150k or below to avoid CFO sign
- Invoice terms: net-60 for pilot, net-30 for annual billing after conversion

Option B — 36mo enterprise commit (CFO + legal sign)
- Consolidated MPO with 10% discount off list pricing
- Requires single consolidated PO by Procurement + CFO approval if total >$150k
- Includes annual true-up clause and SLA addendum

Option C — Pilot then convert
- 3mo paid pilot under PO, then convert to Option B within 30 days of pilot end
- Pilot invoices net-60; conversion documents provided ahead of pilot end to accelerate routing

I attached a redlined offer doc with the three paths (Acme_Offer_Options_20261004.pdf). If you can flag the likely dollar band and confirm whether procurement wants separate POs per BU, I’ll lock the MPO payload and generate the AWS private-offer link and acceptance text.

If Sara (cc’d) should be looped in earlier, happy to include a short one-pager just for finance that summarizes cashflow/true-up.

Thanks — Jordan
